title: Add sdlc stat path inspection command
objective: Add a read-only sdlc stat --path <file-path> command that returns one stable JSON structure for any tracked file path regardless of object type.

branch.name: main
branch.rationale: The repository is already on the main branch and the user requested preparation and commit of the next work item on the current repository.

request.text:
Prepare a new sdlc command:

sdlc stat --path <file-path>

this stat's a file path tracked by the sdlc app/conventions. It doesn't matter what type of object it is, it returns the same json structure.

Write a new .docs/work-items/* -- commit the work item.

scope.name: stat-command
scope.description: Add sdlc stat --path <file-path> as a read-only tracked-path inspection command.
scope.reason: Users need one command boundary for inspecting files tracked by the sdlc application conventions.

scope.name: stable-stat-envelope
scope.description: Return the same top-level JSON response structure for every supported file/object type, including path identity, tracking state, object kind, and bounded stat metadata.
scope.reason: Consumers must be able to parse stat responses without type-specific response branching.

nonGoals.name: tracked-file-mutation
nonGoals.description: Do not write, update, format, migrate, or repair the requested file or its tracking records.
nonGoals.reason: The stat command is an observational read-only boundary.

nonGoals.name: object-specific-contracts
nonGoals.description: Do not create separate response schemas or command routes for individual file/object types in this work item.
nonGoals.reason: The requested behavior requires one invariant JSON structure regardless of object type.

nonGoals.name: provider-and-production-runtime
nonGoals.description: Do not add provider calls, HTTP services, persistence, deployment, or production release behavior.
nonGoals.reason: WI-0004 is limited to local tracked-path inspection and terminal serialization.

items.name: stat-path-option
items.description: sdlc stat must accept --path <file-path> as its explicit path option and provide stable missing, duplicate, invalid, and unknown option errors.
items.reason: The command must have a deterministic and extensible CLI contract.

acceptanceCriteria.description: The command help documents sdlc stat --path <file-path>, and a valid path invocation returns exit code zero for a tracked file.
Missing, duplicate, unknown, absolute, and repository-escaping path inputs return stable non-zero errors without writing files.

items.name: stable-stat-json
items.description: Valid sdlc stat output must use one stable JSON structure regardless of the inspected file/object type.
items.reason: Downstream consumers need one response envelope even when inspected content varies.

acceptanceCriteria.description: JSON output contains a stable schema identifier, requested path, repository-relative path, tracking state, object kind, and bounded stat metadata for each supported file/object fixture.
The response top-level keys and JSON types remain identical across at least two different tracked file/object types.

items.name: stat-read-only-tests
items.description: Focused tests must cover valid tracked paths, object-type neutrality, option errors, path containment, deterministic output, and unchanged filesystem bytes.
items.reason: The command is observational and must not mutate tracked files or records while reporting their state.

acceptanceCriteria.description: yarn test passes with focused stat command coverage and the test fixtures are unchanged after command execution.
